minutes.headline: PACC approved its FY26 budget and a warrant article for Town Meeting, to be filed the next day.
minutes.summary: A special meeting of the Public Access Cable Committee covered only the FY26 budget. Members reviewed salaries, operating expenses, capital and projected income, then voted to accept the budget and the proposed warrant article. They also discussed declining Comcast franchise fee revenue, the Bartholomew investment account, and a streaming bill and PowerPoint for the annual presentation.

votes.motion: Accept the FY26 budget as prepared by Steve and Joe.
Accept the proposed warrant article for the FY26 PEG access Enterprise operating and capital budgets.
Roll call on the warrant article.

budget_items.what_was_said: Salaries for benefited employees and videographers rose over last year because more meetings are being covered. Longevity is included.
Lines for the school building lease, vendors, purchase of services, consultants, advertising, supplies and equipment maintenance are mostly the same as last year.
Capital is held for emergencies and kept separate from equipment maintenance.
The town has not provided indirect costs, so last year's numbers were used as a placeholder. They cover items such as health care, social security and pension.
Operating expenses without capital, with capital, and the overall total for the year were stated, though the captions garble the totals.
A member repeated his annual objection to the rent, but it must be included in the budget format.
Quarterly Comcast payments are declining as people drop cable and keep internet. The average for calendar 2024 fell from 2023, and a 2025 projection continues the decline.
Estimated FY26 income was confirmed as accurate as can be managed.
The account has grown since the initial deposit, and projected interest through June 2025 is used as income. It is a variable rate and not guaranteed.
The committee gets about the same yearly amount from the town, presumed to be interest on the enterprise fund balance. A retained earnings line is left blank pending a question to the town.
A total income figure was stated, though the captions garble it.
The PowerPoint explains that PACC is self-funded from the Comcast franchise fee. The ARPA plan was executed on videographer kits, studio cameras and broadcast audio.
A bill to fund community media through a fee on streaming companies did not pass last session but was not killed. Members want legislators to co-sign.
The proposed warrant asks the town to raise and appropriate or transfer from available funds a sum for the FY26 PEG access enterprise operating and capital budgets.

decisions.decision: The warrant article is to be submitted to Town Hall that night so it is stamped January 20 and in by the deadline.
Indirect costs will be removed from the PowerPoint unless the town or finance department supplies actual figures.
The retained earnings line is left blank for now, and the committee will ask the town how to treat it.

what_happened.line: The Public Access Cable Committee voted to accept its FY26 budget, as prepared by two members.
A motion to accept the warrant article for the FY26 PEG access enterprise operating and capital budgets was made; the result and roll call were not audible.
The committee decided to file the warrant article at Town Hall that night so it is stamped January 20 and meets the deadline.
Members noted quarterly Comcast franchise fee payments are declining as people drop cable, and the 2025 projection continues that decline.
Indirect costs were not supplied by the town, so last year's were used as a placeholder; the retained earnings line was left blank pending a question to the town.

why_it_matters: PACC is funded by the Comcast franchise fee rather than the general tax levy, so falling cable subscriptions shrink the money available for meeting coverage and equipment.
The warrant article is what Town Meeting is asked to vote on for the PEG access operating and capital budgets, but the minutes do not record how the committee voted on it.
watch_next: The warrant article's filing at Town Hall on January 20, and its place on the Town Meeting warrant.
The town's answer on how to treat retained earnings and on actual indirect cost figures.
